per_option_rationale.rationale: Computed C(7, 3) = 35 instead of P(7, 3), dividing by 3! to remove order when order should be kept.
Computed P(7, 4) = 7 x 6 x 5 x 4 = 840 by selecting 4 objects instead of 3.
Computed 7 x 5 x 3 = 105, multiplying every other integer from 7 downward instead of three consecutive integers 7 x 6 x 5.

explanation_sections.punchline: P(7,3) counts ordered selections of 3 from 7: 7 x 6 x 5 = 210.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify as a direct permutation formula application. P(n, r) = n x (n-1) x ... x (n-r+1). Here: 7 x 6 x 5 = 210. Do not divide by r! - that would give combinations, not permutations.
explanation_sections.lesson: P(n, r) = n x (n-1) x ... x (n-r+1): take r consecutive factors starting from n. Never divide by r! when order matters.
explanation_sections.timing: 20-25 s. The instant trap is dividing by 3! = 6, which gives 35 = C(7,3). If order matters, do not divide.
